pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, parallel-group trial with 52-week common double-blind period and variable double-blind period of up to 52 additional weeks
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Biochemical response at Week 52 defined as ALP <1.67×ULN and TB ≤ULN and ALP decrease ≥15% (primary); ALP normalization (ALP ≤1.0×ULN) at Week 52 (key secondary)
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint: biochemical response rate 50.9% (elafibranor) vs 3.8% (placebo); risk difference 47.2% (95% CI: 32.0, 56.9); CMH OR 37.6 (95% CI: 7.6, 302.2); p<0.0001. Key secondary ALP normalization: 14.8% vs 0%; risk difference 14.8% (95% CI: 6.1, 22.7); p=0.0019. Pruritus endpoints not statistically significant.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter dose-finding trial; 12 weeks of treatment; 1:1:1 randomization
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Relative change from baseline in serum ALP levels at Week 12 or end of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: Elafibranor 80 mg: mean ALP percent change -48.3% vs placebo +3.2%; treatment effect vs placebo -52.0% (95% CI: -62.5, -41.5); p<0.001. Elafibranor 120 mg: mean ALP percent change -40.6%; treatment effect -43.9% (95% CI: -55.7, -32.1); p<0.001. Confirmatory evidence supporting Phase 3 dose selection.

key_safety: In the pivotal Phase 3 trial (N=161), key adverse reactions included myalgia/myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (rhabdomyolysis 1.9% vs 0%; myalgia or CPK elevation 7.4% vs 1.9%), fractures (6.5% vs 0%), cholelithiasis/cholecystitis (4% vs 0% and 2% vs 0%, respectively), drug-induced liver injury (3 possible cases across PBC and NASH trials), vomiting (11.1% vs 1.9%), and weight gain >5% from baseline (23.1% vs 20.8%), with pre- and postnatal developmental toxicity observed in rats at exposures approximately equal to or below human therapeutic exposure.
target_moa: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) agonist; activates PPARα and PPARδ (and PPARγ), inhibiting bile acid synthesis and reducing alkaline phosphatase; precise mechanism in PBC not fully established

_meta.indication:
IQIRVO is indicated for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA) in adults who have had an inadequate response to UDCA, or as monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA.
This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on reduction of alkaline phosphatase (ALP). Improvement in survival or prevention of liver decompensation events have not been demonstrated. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trial(s).
Limitations of Use:
Use of IQIRVO is not recommended in patients who have or develop decompensated cirrhosis (e.g., ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy).

indication_details.population_restrictions: adults; patients with primary biliary cholangitis (PBC); not recommended in patients who have or develop decompensated cirrhosis
indication_details.combination: in combination with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), or monotherapy in patients unable to tolerate UDCA
indication_details.prior_therapy_required: prior UDCA therapy with inadequate response, or inability to tolerate UDCA
